To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we can identify subnetworks of BERT that disentangle the representations of syntax and sentiment from the representations of semantics and genre, and that these disentangled representations can be used to perform as well or better than previously reported methods for disentanglement.

(1) we can disentangle the syntactic and semantic representations of BERT by learning binary masks over the weights of a transformer layer, and that (2) these masks are quite sparse, and (3) that the masked subnetworks perform as well as or even better than previously proposed models that explicitly disentangle representations.

We propose a method to disentangled representations in large pre-trained language models by identifying subnetwork that encode distinct, predictive aspects of the representation and evaluate it on a variety of tasks.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following question: How can we disentangle the representations in pre-trained models, which encode a variety of features, to obtain a better understanding of their internal workings and to improve the interpretability of the representations?
